# GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98 fixtures

These files were reduced from a real `events.jsonl` that Copilot 1.0.98 wrote against a local fake OpenAI-compatible provider (`COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, a scratch `COPILOT_HOME`), so nothing was sent to GitHub. Ids are synthetic, paths are `/home/user/...`, the system prompt is left out. Nothing here is a credential, and cornercase never reads `config.json` or anything in `COPILOT_HOME` but the files named below.

**Which session is a pane's.** `<home>/session-state/<id>/` holds `events.jsonl` (created with the first prompt), `workspace.yaml` (not read) and `inuse.<pid>.lock` and `inuse.<pid>.hold`. The process holds the `.hold` file open for as long as it lives, so a pane's session is the folder whose `inuse.<pid>.hold` is among the files that pid (or its Copilot child under the npm loader or `gh copilot`) has open. A lock left by a process that was killed is never held, so it is ignored. The package folder under `~/.cache/copilot/pkg/` has its own `inuse.<pid>.hold`, which does not count: only one directly under `session-state/<id>/` does. These files depend on the pid, so the fake creates them at run time and no fixture holds them.

**Working or not.** `open-sessions-state.json` is an object keyed by session id with a `working` boolean. Copilot rewrites it, so a read that does not parse keeps the previous value. A session killed with `kill -9` leaves its entry behind with `working: false` (the second entry in the fixture). `working` stays true after the last `assistant.turn_end` while a background shell started with `mode: "async"` runs (live: 25 s), and goes false once it has finished; `system.notification` with `kind.type` `shell_completed` is written when it ends.

**Events.** One `assistant.turn_start`/`assistant.turn_end` pair is one model call, so a prompt gives several pairs and they do not end the work. `abort` (`user_initiated` for Ctrl+C, `user_abort` for Esc) is written after the turn's `assistant.turn_end`. Ephemeral events are never written: `session.idle`, `session.usage_info`, `user_input.requested`, `exit_plan_mode.requested` and the rest.

**Waiting.** An open `permission.requested` (until its `permission.completed`), and an open `tool.execution_start` for `ask_user` or `exit_plan_mode` (until `tool.execution_complete` or the `human_response.recorded` that answers it), mean the agent needs you. The plan review is `exit_plan_mode`: live, its `tool.execution_start` stayed open until the plan was accepted or cancelled.

**Prompts.** A `user.message` is a prompt unless it has a `source` (skills, other agents), `isAutopilotContinuation: true` or `agentMode: "shell"`. `delivery` is `idle`, `steering` or `queued`; a prompt typed while a turn runs is written, with `queued`, when Copilot takes it. `/help`, `!command` and a lone `?` write no `user.message` at all; `? text` writes one with the text after the `?`.

**Replies.** The last message is the newest `assistant.message` with non-empty `content` and no `parentToolCallId`; chunks of one `apiCallId` (`chunkIndex`, `chunkCount`) are joined in order. `reasoningText` and `encryptedContent` are never read.

**Model and context.** The model is `selectedModel` of `session.start`/`session.resume`, `newModel` of `session.model_change`, `chosenModel` of `session.auto_mode_resolved` or the `model` of the newest main reply; with `auto` selected it shows `auto` until a concrete one is known. The percentage is the newest main `session.usage_record` as `inputTokens / maxPromptTokens`. A record is the main agent's unless it has a `parentToolCallId`, an `initiator` of `sub-agent` or `mcp-sampling`, or an `interactionType` other than `conversation-agent`. `session.compaction_complete` (when it succeeded), `session.truncation`, `session.context_cleared` and a `session.model_change` that is not the startup one hide it until the next main record.

**Tokens.** `inputTokens` includes what the cache served (live: a provider answering `prompt_tokens` 12345 with 2000 cached gave `inputTokens` 12345 and `cacheReadTokens` 2000), so Stats count `inputTokens - cacheReadTokens - cacheWriteTokens` as input. `reasoningTokens` is part of the output. Every usage record counts, sub-agents' too, once by its event `id`; only main records move the percentage.

`trust.txt` is the folder question, reduced to a narrower box. It matches the default trust pattern (`do you trust`), and Enter picks the highlighted `1. Yes`.

**Sub-agents.** `subagent.started` (`toolCallId`, `agentName`, optional `executionMode` `sync` or `background`) opens one and `subagent.completed` (with `cancelled: true` when an abort or an ancestor being killed tore it down) or `subagent.failed` closes it, both by `toolCallId`; events of the sub-agent itself carry that id as `parentToolCallId` (`data.parentToolCallId`, or `data.usage.parentToolCallId` in a `session.usage_record`). `session.start`, `session.resume` and `session.shutdown` forget them all. **`subagent-*.jsonl` were built from the 1.0.98 `session-events.schema.json` and Copilot's own code, not captured in a live run.**
